_comment: Manual scores for the two items score.py cannot compute. t1.d_judged max 4 (does the answer name the median-vs-tail flaw?), t4.prose_judged max 3 (is the report worth reading?). Empty/errored runs score 0.

_schema.keys: Each '<task>.<item>' table accepts two key forms, tried in this order.
_schema.1_per_rep: '<model>#rep<n>' — the judgement for ONE rep, e.g. 'gpt-oss:20b#rep2'. Prefer this: each rep produces a different answer.txt, so each rep needs its own judgement.
_schema.2_legacy_model_only: '<model>' — applies to every rep of that model. Predates reps; kept so judgements made before the per-rep change are not lost. score.py honours it but records a note that the score was inherited rather than judged for that rep.
_schema.missing: A model/rep in neither form is reported as judged_pending and appears in the --all worklist. It is NOT scored 0: unjudged and zero are different, and the roll-up marks any total with a pending item as PROVISIONAL.
_schema.note: Entries below are all legacy model-only keys, made 2026-08-08 against rep 1. They have deliberately not been rewritten as per-rep keys, because doing so would assert they describe rep 2 as well, which nobody has checked.
_schema.judged_2026_08_11: The 26 per-rep entries added 2026-08-11 were scored against the existing model-level judgements as calibration: t1 4 = names the median-vs-tail flaw crisply, 3 = right idea without naming a percentile, 2 = a genuine but different flaw (latency vs throughput), 0 = empty or errored. t4 3 = concrete and specific, 2.5 = strong with a defect, 2 = readable but thin, 1 = stub, 0 = no report.md written.
